entities.summary: Reginald Leslie "Snowy" Baker was an Australian athlete, sports promoter, and actor. Born in Surry Hills, an inner-city suburb of Sydney, New South Wales, Baker excelled at a number of sports, winning New South Wales swimming and boxing championships while still a teenager. Playing rugby union for Eastern Suburbs, he played several games for New South Wales against Queensland, and in 1904 represented Australia in two Test matches against Great Britain. At the 1908 London Olympics, Baker represented Australasia in swimming and diving, as well as taking part in the middleweight boxing event, in which he won a silver medal.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Australian athlete and actor, Reginald Baker's achievements in sports and entertainment contributed to the development of Australasian identity during the early 20th century. His Olympic medal-winning performance in boxing helped pave the way for future generations of Australian athletes.
